> Align protein sequences pairwise with mzLib's global affine-gap aligner, and map every residue of each sequence to its counterpart in the other, or to none.

Wire verb `proteins align` · Python [`pymzlib.proteins.align_many`][pymzlib.proteins.align_many]

### Wraps

- [`PairwiseAligner`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs) in `mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`PairwiseAligner.Align`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs) in `mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`PairwiseAligner.Id`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs) in `mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`PairwiseAlignment.TryMapSourceToTarget`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAlignment.cs) in `mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAlignment.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`PairwiseAlignment.TryMapTargetToSource`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAlignment.cs) in `mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAlignment.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pairs` | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 pair; each line exactly one tab` | Read from stdin (not an option): one pair per line, the source sequence, a tab, the target sequence, as one-letter residue codes. Each sequence reaches mzLib exactly as given, case and all. Either sequence may be empty, but not both, because a blank line is skipped. One row per line, in input order, duplicates included. Sequences always travel on stdin, never argv: two titin isoforms are about 70,000 characters, past argv's 32 KB ceiling on Windows. |
| `gap_open` (wire `--gap-open`) | `int` | `11` | half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units) | `>= 0 (mzLib refuses a negative value)` | The cost of opening a gap, charged once per gap. A gap of length k costs gap-open plus k times gap-extend, BLAST's convention. Absent: nothing is sent and mzLib's PairwiseAligner default applies, which is 11 at d10017ce (BLASTP's default with BLOSUM62). |
| `gap_extend` (wire `--gap-extend`) | `int` | `1` | half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units) | `>= 1 (mzLib refuses 0 or less)` | The cost of each residue in a gap, the first included. Absent: mzLib's default, 1 at d10017ce. |
| `end_gaps` (wire `--end-gaps`) | `string` | `free` | — | `free \| charged (case-insensitive)` | free: a gap at either end of either sequence costs nothing, so one sequence may overhang the other (a signal peptide, a longer C-terminus) without penalty, as EMBOSS needle scores end gaps by default. charged: every gap costs. mzLib's PairwiseAligner.FreeEndGaps, true or false. Absent: mzLib's default, free (true) at d10017ce. The spelling is mzLib's own, from its aligner id. |
| `max_cells` (wire `--max-cells`) | `int` | `200000000` | cells | `1 to 2147483591 (Array.MaxLength; mzLib refuses anything outside)` | The largest dynamic-programming table mzLib will build, (source length + 1) x (target length + 1) cells of one byte each. A larger pair is refused rather than allowed to exhaust memory. Absent: mzLib's default, 200,000,000 cells (about 200 MB) at d10017ce. |
| `no_residue_map` (wire `--no-residue-map`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Leave out the residue map (residue_map is then null). The pairs table is unchanged. For a batch where only the scores and counts are wanted: the map has one row per residue of both sequences. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aligner_id` | `string` | — | never | mzLib's PairwiseAligner.Id, naming the method and every parameter, e.g. global-affine;BLOSUM62;open=11;extend=1;end-gaps=free. Store it with any mapped position. |
| `matrix` | `string` | — | never | The substitution matrix's name, always BLOSUM62: mzLib's default, the only one the wire offers. |
| `gap_open` | `int` | half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units) | never | The gap-open cost the aligner used: the option's value, or mzLib's default when it was absent. |
| `gap_extend` | `int` | half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units) | never | The gap-extension cost the aligner used. |
| `end_gaps` | `string` | — | never | free or charged: the end-gap rule the aligner used. |
| `max_cells` | `int` | cells | never | The table limit the aligner used. |
| `record_count` | `int` | pairs | never | Rows: the input pairs. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | The pairs table's columns in order. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | Column name to one value per pair, in input order. |
| `residue_map` | `object` | — | yes: --no-residue-map was given | {row_count, column_names, columns}: one row per residue of each sequence of each pair, pair by pair, each pair's source residues (positions 1 to its length) and then its target residues (typed under result.tables.residue_map). |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Seven static caveats. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pair_index` | `int` | — | never | 0-based position of the pair among the non-blank stdin lines. |
| `source_length` | `int` | residues | never | The source sequence's length. |
| `target_length` | `int` | residues | never | The target sequence's length. |
| `score` | `int` | half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units) | never | PairwiseAlignment.Score: substitution scores summed over the paired residues, less every charged gap. A raw score, not a bit score, an E-value or an identity; compare it only between alignments with the same aligner_id. |
| `identical` | `int` | residues | never | Paired residues that are the same letter, compared case-insensitively (PairwiseAlignment.Identical). |
| `substituted` | `int` | residues | never | Paired residues that differ (PairwiseAlignment.Substituted). |
| `source_residues_facing_gap` | `int` | residues | never | Source residues with no target counterpart: an extra or deleted stretch, or an overhang. |
| `target_residues_facing_gap` | `int` | residues | never | Target residues with no source counterpart. |
| `aligned_source` | `string` | — | never | The source as given with '-' wherever it faces a target residue across a gap; as long as aligned_target. |
| `aligned_target` | `string` | — | never | The target as given with '-' wherever it faces a source residue across a gap. |

Fields of `residue_map`:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pair_index` | `int` | — | never | The pair the residue belongs to. |
| `sequence` | `string` | — | never | source or target: which sequence position is in. |
| `position` | `int` | — | never | 1-based position in that sequence, as everywhere in mzLib. |
| `residue` | `string` | — | never | The residue at position, one letter, as given. |
| `mapped_position` | `int` | — | yes: the residue faces a gap, so it has no counterpart (mzLib's TryMap returned false); never the nearest residue | 1-based position of the paired residue in the other sequence: TryMapSourceToTarget for a source row, TryMapTargetToSource for a target row. |
| `mapped_residue` | `string` | — | yes: the residue faces a gap | The paired residue, one letter, as given. Different from residue on a substitution. |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | no pairs on stdin; a line that is not exactly two tab-separated fields (the message names the pair) |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | --gap-open, --gap-extend or --max-cells not an integer, or given without a value; a value mzLib's PairwiseAligner constructor refuses (gap-open below 0, gap-extend below 1, max-cells below 1 or above 2147483591), with mzLib's message and the option named; --end-gaps not free or charged, or given without a value |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | mzLib refused a pair: a sequence holding a gap character ('-' or '.'), or a table larger than max-cells. The message names the pair and quotes mzLib, which gives the cell count. The whole call fails on the first such pair, in input order. |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | never seen at d10017ce: mzLib's aligner throws nothing else for non-null input |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | never raised by this verb |

### Caveats

- score is a raw substitution-matrix score in BLOSUM62's half-bit units, summed over the alignment: it grows with length and is not a bit score, an E-value or a percent identity. Compare scores only between alignments with the same aligner_id.
- Global alignment: every residue of both sequences is in the alignment, paired or facing a gap. With end gaps free (mzLib's default) an overhang at either end costs nothing, so a short sequence is placed on the best-scoring stretch of a long one even when it has no real match there.
- A residue facing a gap has no counterpart: its mapped_position is null, never the nearest residue.
- One optimal alignment is returned. Where several score the same, mzLib's traceback prefers a residue pair, then a gap in the target, then a gap in the source, so the same input always gives the same alignment; a residue beside an indel may sit on the other side of the gap in another aligner's equally good answer. DYNC1I2 isoform 2B lacks six residues of the canonical sequence: V76 and V82 of the canonical are both V, either could pair with the isoform's V76, and mzLib pairs V82.
- mzLib refuses only the gap characters '-' and '.'. Any other character BLOSUM62 does not name (selenocysteine U, pyrrolysine O, J, a digit, a space, a bracket) is scored as X, so pass bare one-letter sequences. Letters are compared case-insensitively; aligned_source, aligned_target and the residue columns keep the case given.
- Time and memory grow with the product of the two lengths: mzLib builds a (source length + 1) x (target length + 1) table of one byte per cell and refuses a pair larger than max_cells. Two identical sequences free of X and * are aligned residue for residue without the table, so max_cells does not limit them.
- Each stdin line is one pair, aligned in input order; blank lines are skipped. mzLib's aligner takes no thread count, so pairs are aligned one after another.

### Example

```python
aln = pymzlib.proteins.align('MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ', 'MKTAYIAKISFVKSHFSRQ')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`proteins_align_deletion.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/proteins_align_deletion.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

```python
alns = pymzlib.proteins.align_many([('MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ', 'MKTAYIAKISFVKSHFSRQ'), ('MLLLPEPTIDE', 'PEPTIDE')])
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`proteins_align_many.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/proteins_align_many.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

```python
charged = pymzlib.proteins.align('MLLLPEPTIDE', 'PEPTIDE', end_gaps='charged')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`proteins_align_charged.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/proteins_align_charged.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

### References

- [doi:10.1016/0022-2836(70)90057-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-2836(70)90057-4): Global alignment by dynamic programming (Needleman and Wunsch 1970, J Mol Biol 48:443)
- [doi:10.1016/0022-2836(82)90398-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-2836(82)90398-9): Affine gap costs in the same time and memory order, the form mzLib implements (Gotoh 1982, J Mol Biol 162:705)
- [doi:10.1073/pnas.89.22.10915](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.89.22.10915): BLOSUM62, the substitution matrix and its half-bit units (Henikoff and Henikoff 1992, PNAS 89:10915)

!!! warning "Not yet verified"

    - A substitution matrix other than BLOSUM62 is not offered. mzLib can read one (SubstitutionMatrix.Parse(name, TextReader), NCBI's text format), but it needs a name for the aligner id, which the bridge would have to invent, and the units of every score would then be that matrix's. Whether to add --matrix FILE, and where its name comes from, is open.
    - mzLib scores any character BLOSUM62 does not name as X, digits and spaces included, so a sequence with a stray modification bracket or a number aligns without complaint. Whether PairwiseAligner.Align should refuse non-letters, as it refuses '-' and '.', is an mzLib question, not raised upstream yet.
    - Pairs are aligned one at a time: PairwiseAligner takes no degree of parallelism, so the wire has no --threads (PARALLELISM.md). A batch aligner with one (for proteome-wide ortholog or isoform maps) would be an mzLib addition.
    - residue_map is not validated by tools/check_verbs.py, which checks only 'columns' and 'bulk'. The bridge test ADeletion_LeavesItsResiduesUnmappedAndMapsAcrossTheGap pins its column order.
    - Not yet ported to mzLibRust or mzLibR; the binding names above are proposals.
